questions.explain: Legitimate: resilience with real independence, M&A reality, best-of-breed services, commercial leverage. Illegitimate: resume-driven architecture and vague 'avoiding lock-in' without a threat model.
options: Regulatory requirement for a second provider
Post-acquisition estates on different clouds
Credible leverage for pricing negotiations
Vague 'avoiding lock-in' with no threat model, or resume-driven architecture
questions.q: Which of these is NOT a legitimate reason to go multi-cloud, per Chapter 24?

questions.explain: Overlapping CIDRs are the most common blocker — two VPCs/VNets both using 10.0.0.0/16 cannot peer or route — so address space must be planned before the first deployment.
options: Expired TLS certificates on the interconnect
Overlapping CIDR address ranges between the clouds' networks
Mismatched SQL Server collations
Different cloud billing currencies
questions.q: What is the most common blocker for cross-cloud private connectivity?

questions.explain: The working consistency models are single-writer (one cloud accepts writes; lag is the only inconsistency) or partitioned writers (each site owns disjoint data); bidirectional replication with conflict resolution is a last resort.
options: Single-writer or partitioned writers; bidirectional conflict resolution is a last resort
Eventual consistency with automatic conflict-free merges
Synchronous replication across clouds for zero divergence
Shared writable storage mounted from both clouds
questions.q: What consistency models does the chapter endorse for SQL Server across clouds?

questions.explain: The pattern is federate, don't duplicate: one identity provider (usually Entra ID for SQL Server estates) federated to each cloud, so a departing DBA loses access everywhere at once.
options: Separate local accounts on each cloud's SQL Server
Duplicating every login in IAM, Entra ID, and Google IAM
One identity provider federated to each cloud — federate, don't duplicate
Shared sa passwords synchronized by email
questions.q: What is the identity pattern for multi-cloud SQL Server estates?

questions.explain: Synchronous replication across clouds is a performance disaster due to latency, and 'we'll figure out failover later' ignores that cross-cloud failover is a business process involving DNS, identity, and app configuration.
options: Workload placement with data flowing via replication or ETL
Synchronous replication across clouds
Active-passive with portable backup artifacts
Active-active with strict write partitioning
questions.q: Which architecture does the chapter say does NOT work in production?

title: Chapter 24: Multi-Cloud Database Strategy: Benefits and Traps
